title: Check yourself: what happens to a request on its way

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A colleague adds a second link. The new adaptor reads acq-send and writes acq-receive, and the new QMUX is given <in>acq-send</in> and <out>acq-receive</out>, copied from the adaptor's file, with <ready> set. The adaptor connects. What does the first purchase sent through this QMUX do?

options.text: It waits out its timeout and returns null, since the QMUX puts it on a queue that only the adaptor writes to
options.says: QMUX's <in> must be the adaptor's <out>; with the names copied, the request sits in acq-receive and never leaves the JVM

options.text: It waits out its timeout and returns null, since the host gets it but the answer is put on the unhandled queue
options.says: the request never reaches the host: nothing reads the queue the QMUX wrote it to

options.text: It fails at once with an ISOException, since QMUX checks when it is deployed that its queues match the adaptor's
options.says: QMUX checks nothing about the adaptor; Q2 deploys it without an error

options.text: It fails at once with an ISOException, since isConnected() stays false while the two sets of queues disagree
options.says: isConnected() only looks at the ready entry, which the adaptor sets, so it is true; and request() does not check it anyway

origin.section: 4.1 QMUX Sits on the Adaptor's Queues, Crossed

questions.stem: The link to the host drops at 12:00:00, and the adaptor reconnects at 12:00:08. At 12:00:03 a thread calls request(purchase, 15000) without asking isConnected() first. What happens to that purchase?

options.text: It goes out once the link is back, since it waits in the send queue for up to 15 seconds, and the thread gets the host's answer
options.says: request() never checks the link; the message waits in the queue with the timeout as its lifetime, and the adaptor sends it after reconnecting

options.text: It goes out once the link is back, since the adaptor replays what it missed, but the thread was already given null at 12:00:03
options.says: request() waits for its full timeout, not until it notices the link; it returns the answer that arrives within the 15 seconds

options.text: It never goes out, since QMUX refuses a request while the ready entry is missing, so the thread gets an ISOException
options.says: only send() refuses on a down link; request() queues the message

options.text: It never goes out, since the adaptor clears its send queue when it reconnects, so the thread gets null after 15 seconds
options.says: the adaptor sends what is still in the queue; a message is lost only if its lifetime runs out first

origin.section: 4.4 A Request on a Down Link Waits in the Queue

questions.stem: A service sends every authorization with the listener form of request() and a 10-second timeout. Each listener stores the response in a database, which takes about 2 seconds, before completing the caller's future. At peak, 30 authorizations are outstanding on one link. What do you expect to see?

options.text: Answers wait to be read while earlier listeners run, so some purchases time out although the host approved them
options.says: the listener runs on the adaptor's receiver thread, the only thread that reads the socket; while it works, no other answer is read

options.text: Answers wait in a queue for a free listener thread, so some purchases take 2 seconds longer but still complete in time
options.says: there is no listener pool: the receiver thread itself runs the listener and reads nothing else meanwhile

options.text: Each listener runs on the thread that sent its request, so some callers wait 2 seconds longer than the host took
options.says: the sending thread returned at once; the listener runs on a jPOS thread, not the caller's

options.text: Each listener runs on a new thread per response, so some database writes overlap while the answers keep flowing
options.says: answers are delivered on the receiver thread; expiries on a QMUX scheduler thread; jPOS does not start a thread per response

origin.section: 4.5 The Asynchronous Form Calls Back Once, With an Answer or With null

questions.stem: host-pool is a MUXPool with the primary-secondary strategy over host-mux and host-mux-b. Both links have been down for a minute. A thread calls request(purchase, 5000) on host-pool. What does it get?

options.text: null after about 5 seconds, since the pool keeps looking for a connected member until the timeout is spent
options.says: with no usable member the pool checks once a second until the timeout runs out, then returns null without sending

options.text: null after about 5 seconds, since the pool hands the purchase to host-mux, whose send queue holds it until it expires
options.says: the pool passes a request only to a usable member; with none, nothing is handed to any QMUX

options.text: an ISOException at once, since the pool refuses a blocking request when none of its members is connected
options.says: the blocking request returns null after the timeout; it is the listener form of the pool that throws, and only after waiting

options.text: an ISOException at once, since primary-secondary requires the first member to be connected before it will send
options.says: primary-secondary picks the first connected member in order, whichever it is; with none it waits and returns null

origin.section: 4.7.1 A Pool Takes the Name's Place

concepts: A response's listener runs on the adaptor's receiver thread, so a slow listener delays every answer on the link.
A MUXPool uses its first connected member under primary-secondary, and with none it keeps checking until the timeout and returns null.
QMUX's in queue is the adaptor's out queue and the other way round; copied unchanged, every request times out without leaving the JVM and without an error.
